records.title: QMS: the /api/qms second door is deleted and every mdx-qms write now needs an editor role, but supplier approval and NC disposition are still unsigned and their audit rows are written after the commit
records.evidenceAtHead: FIXED PART: server/routes/qms.ts and server/services/qms/qms.service.ts no longer exist at HEAD. server/bootstrap/register-document-routes.ts:271-278 is now only the removal note. A grep for a '/api/qms' mount outside tests finds nothing. In server/routes/mdx-qms.ts every write route is gated: 18 carry requireEditorAccess (lines 361, 448, 650, 714, 906, 941, 1019, 1051, 1120, 1182, 1216, 1360, 1401, 1424, 1526, 1563, 1588); /qms/documents/:id/approve (602) and /qms/changes/:id/approve (1482) use verifyApprovalSigner (556) plus a BEGIN/COMMIT signed write; training-ack (757) takes userId from the session (getUserId), not from the body. At 92ccdba1, 16 of the 20 write routes had no requireEditorAccess (git show 92ccdba1:server/routes/mdx-qms.ts | grep -v requireEditorAccess count = 16). OPEN PART: supplierCreate (mdx-qms.ts:873-878) accepts approvalStatus from SUPPLIER_STATUS, 'approved' included. POST /qms/suppliers (906) and PATCH /qms/suppliers/:id (941, COL map at 950: approvalStatus -> approval_status) write it with a plain pool.query and no signature. The audit row comes from recordAuditRow after the committed write (the code's own comment calls it 'a log beside it'). PATCH /qms/nonconforming/:id/disposition (1216) has the same shape: pool.query UPDATE of disposition (scrap/rework/use_as_is), then recordAuditRow, with no signature and no guard against re-dispositioning. Internal-audit PATCH (1051) and management-review POST (1120) are also unsigned. client/src calls only mdx/qms/{documents,changes,templates,training}, with no supplier or nonconforming caller.
records.fixedBy: c6f2028b2 (P1-31/DP-34: deleted server/routes/qms.ts and qms.service.ts, removed the mount at register-document-routes.ts:271, added requireEditorAccess to the supplier/internal-audit/management-review/NC routes in server/routes/mdx-qms.ts:906,941,1019,1051,1120,1182,1216); f1d2589ff (change-control writes need an editor, mdx-qms.ts:1360-1588); cf950eeb9 and 0f961354c (signing authority on the QMS approve routes, mdx-qms.ts:602,1482).
records.remaining: (1) An editor can set a supplier to approved or qualified through POST or PATCH /api/mdx/qms/suppliers with no electronic signature, no signing-authority check and no meaning or reason. (2) An editor can disposition a nonconforming product (use_as_is, scrap) with no signature, and can re-disposition an already-dispositioned NC. (3) For both, the audit row is written after the record commits: if it fails, the decision stands with no audit trail. (4) Internal-audit completion and management reviews are unsigned. (5) Minor: training-ack accepts a self-reported quizScore from the body.
records.severityRationale: The P1 core is closed: the viewer-writable second door is gone and every QMS write needs an editor. The launch-catalog surface, QMS controlled documents, is signed with chained audit. Supplier and NC decisions have no UI in the shipped client, so only an editor calling the API directly can reach them, and the pilot is FDA-only with founder support. They must be signed governed writes before GA to ISO 13485 / 21 CFR 820 medtech buyers.
records.humanTestingNote: Testers cannot see this through the six apps: the client has no supplier or nonconforming-product screen. The only way to reproduce it is by API: as an editor, PATCH /api/mdx/qms/suppliers/:id {"approvalStatus":"approved"} returns 200 with no signature prompt.
records.instructions:
1. server/routes/mdx-qms.ts:873-886: remove approvalStatus and approvalDate from supplierCreate, and therefore from supplierPatch, which is supplierCreate.partial(). In the PATCH COL map at line 950, drop approvalStatus and approvalDate. POST /qms/suppliers (906) then always inserts 'pending' (the COALESCE($6,'pending') becomes the literal 'pending'). A body that still carries approvalStatus is answered 422 with code SUPPLIER_STANDING_REQUIRES_SIGNATURE. Do not silently ignore it.
2. Add POST /qms/suppliers/:id/approval with body {approvalStatus: 'approved'|'conditional'|'disqualified'|..., reason, meaning, password, totp?}. Copy the /qms/changes/:id/approve handler (1482-1524): getUserId, verifyApprovalSigner(res, userId, orgId, body) (556), pool.connect, BEGIN, then a new service function approveQmsSupplierSigned(client, {...}) in server/services/qms/supplier-approval-signature.ts, modelled on server/services/qms/change-approval-signature.ts:157 approveQmsChangeSigned. Inside the transaction that function must: UPDATE qms_suppliers SET approval_status, approval_date=now() WHERE id AND organization_id AND deleted_at IS NULL (404 when no row); persist the signature through the same signature persistence approveQmsChangeSigned uses; and write the chained audit row in the same client. Then COMMIT, with ROLLBACK on any throw.
3. Replace PATCH /qms/nonconforming/:id/disposition (1216-1240) with a signed POST /qms/nonconforming/:id/disposition that follows the same ceremony (verifyApprovalSigner, transaction, signature, chained audit row in the same transaction). Refuse with 409 when disposition is already not 'pending' unless the body carries reopen:true plus a reason. Removing the PATCH removes no user-facing capability, because no client calls it (client/src greps clean). Name the new POST route in the commit message as the replacement.
4. For PATCH /qms/internal-audits/:id (1051) when status moves to completed, and for POST /qms/management-reviews (1120): at minimum, wrap the write and a writeChainedAuditRow (server/services/auditService.ts:269) in one pool.connect transaction instead of recordAuditRow after commit.
5. Tests, written and seen to fail first: add server/routes/__tests__/mdx-qms-supplier-nc-signed.test.ts with these cases. (a) Editor PATCH /api/mdx/qms/suppliers/:id {approvalStatus:'approved'} returns 422 and the row is unchanged; this returns 200 at HEAD. (b) POST /qms/suppliers/:id/approval with no password returns 4xx and nothing is written. (c) With a valid signature it returns 200, writes one signature row and one chained audit_logs row, and approval_status is 'approved'. (d) With the audit insert forced to throw, the request returns 500 and approval_status is still the old value. Write the same four cases for NC disposition. Run each red on HEAD, then green.
6. Run npm run ci:sign-ceremony and npm run ci:discarded-audit-write. The new routes must pass, and the baselines must shrink, not grow.
records.acceptance: A viewer and an editor both get 422/403 when they try to change supplier approval_status or NC disposition through the unsigned routes, and the row is unchanged (failing first: 200 at HEAD). The signed routes return 200 only with a verified signature, write a signature row and a chained audit_logs row in the same transaction, and roll back completely when the audit write fails. Re-dispositioning a dispositioned NC returns 409. ci:sign-ceremony passes with no new baseline entries.
records.dependencies: None. Reuses verifyApprovalSigner (server/routes/mdx-qms.ts:556) and the change-approval-signature.ts ceremony.

records.title: Legacy /api/projects: DELETE now needs an editor and refuses to delete records, but POST and PATCH have no role gate and the delete and update audit rows are unattributed (userId null), unchained and written after commit
records.evidenceAtHead: server/routes/projects-management.ts at HEAD: DELETE at 341 is `router.delete('/:projectId', requireEditorAccess, ...)`. Lines 369-379 run db.transaction with projectDeletionHolds and projectDeletionRefusal (server/services/c2c/project-retention.ts:55-131). These lock the rows and refuse with 409 for the anchor of a live program or any artifact past draft, signed, snapshotted or carrying review comments. Still open: POST '/' (153) and PATCH '/:projectId' (433) carry no role middleware. The router has no router.use gate (line 38), and the mount at server/bootstrap/register-project-routes.ts:32-33 adds none. The DELETE audit (383-414) is a plain db.insert(auditEvents) after the transaction commits, with `userId: null` at 391, inside a try/catch that only logs (411). The PATCH audit has `userId: null` at 479 and a swallowed catch at 499. The PATCH UPDATE (~460) filters by id only; the org check is the read before it. At 92ccdba1 none of POST/DELETE/PATCH (150/336/408) had a role gate. Reachability: client/src only GETs /api/projects (TaskBoard.tsx:326,1485,1673; CollabLauncher.tsx:173). The shipped Projects app writes through /api/c2c/projects (register-inline-routes.ts:851), whose mutations are authorized by canMutateProgram (server/services/c2c/program-access.ts).
records.fixedBy: 2b33033e4 and 9109aa770 (PF-08/PF-13: requireEditorAccess on DELETE, projectDeletionHolds in the deleting transaction, server/routes/projects-management.ts:341,369-379; server/services/c2c/project-retention.ts); 0ecc058c5 (database refusal answered 409, projects-management.ts:419-425).
records.remaining: (1) A viewer can POST a new project and PATCH any project in the org (name, description, status including 'archived', priority) by direct API call. This includes a regulatory program's anchor row. (2) DELETE and PATCH audit rows are not attributable: userId is null, and only userName is filled from getRequestActor. They are plain audit_events rows rather than chained, written after commit, and a failed write is swallowed. POST's audit (312) is likewise swallowed. (3) Deleting a drafts-only project still hard-cascades non-governed children (tasks, review threads, report_os_*) with no legal-hold check.
records.severityRationale: The destructive half of the P1 is closed: a viewer can no longer delete, and no delete can cascade away records. What remains is role over-permission on non-destructive metadata writes to a legacy table the shipped UI only reads, plus Part 11 attributability gaps in its audit rows. That is real before GA, but it does not stop an invited-org pilot.
records.humanTestingNote: Testers cannot see this through the UI: the Projects app creates, edits and deletes through /api/c2c/projects, and the client only reads /api/projects. It can only be reproduced by API: as a viewer, PATCH /api/projects/:id {"status":"archived"} returns 200.
records.instructions:
1. server/routes/projects-management.ts: import requireEditorAccessForWrites and governedActorId from '../middleware/orgMembership' (line 11 already imports requireEditorAccess). Add `router.use(requireEditorAccessForWrites);` directly after `const router = Router();` (line 38), so POST, PATCH, DELETE and any future write need a writing role while GET stays open to viewers.
2. DELETE (341-431): before opening the transaction, read `const actorId = governedActorId(req)` and return 401 when it is null. Inside the db.transaction at 369, after `tx.delete(...)` succeeds, call `await writeChainedAuditRow(queryableFromDrizzle(tx), { tenantId: organizationId, userId: actorId, action: 'project_delete', resourceType: 'project', resourceId: String(projectId), details: { oldValues: existingProject, reason: 'Project deleted' } })` (server/services/auditService.ts:269). Delete the post-commit auditEvents insert and its swallowed catch (383-414). An audit failure then throws, the transaction rolls back, and the handler answers 500 with nothing deleted.
3. PATCH (433-520): wrap the UPDATE and a writeChainedAuditRow (action 'project_update', userId governedActorId(req), details {changedFields, oldValues, newValues}) in one db.transaction. Add `and(eq(projects.id, projectId), eq(projects.organizationId, organizationId))` to the UPDATE where-clause, and remove the swallowed-catch insert at ~466-501.
4. POST (153-330): replace the swallowed catch at 312 with the same chained write. Run it in the same transaction if atomicCreateProject (server/services/atomicQuotaService.js) can take a client; otherwise fail the response with 500 and an explicit `auditTrail: {persisted:false}`. Never return 201 silently.
5. Tests, seen to fail first: add server/routes/__tests__/projects-management-governed-writes.test.ts modelled on server/routes/__tests__/device-projects-delete-ownership.test.ts. (a) A viewer gets 403 on POST, PATCH and DELETE and nothing changes; POST and PATCH return 2xx at HEAD. (b) An editor DELETE of a drafts-only project writes one audit_logs row whose actor_id equals the session user and whose chain fields are set. (c) With writeChainedAuditRow forced to throw, DELETE returns 500 and the project row still exists. Run red on HEAD, then green.
6. Extend scripts/ci/check-regulated-delete-audit.mjs to refuse an audit insert in a delete handler whose user field is the literal null. Show its selftest failing on projects-management.ts:391 before the fix.
records.acceptance: A viewer gets 403 on POST, PATCH and DELETE /api/projects (failing first: 2xx for POST and PATCH at HEAD). Every successful project update or delete has exactly one chained audit_logs row carrying the session user id, written in the same transaction. A forced audit failure leaves the project unchanged and returns 500. ci:regulated-delete-audit fails on a null-user delete audit (selftest shown red), and passes after the fix.

records.title: MCP connector: bearer and grant checks now go through verifyLiveToken and registration fails closed in production, but tenant lifecycle (read-only and deny states other than 'suspended'), refresh-token reuse detection and consent re-authentication are still open. The connector is now enabled in Terraform.
records.evidenceAtHead: FIXED: server/mcp/auth/platform-token.ts:122-145 decodeAccessClaims now calls verifyLiveToken (134). That is server/services/token-revocation.ts:289-313: revocation list, account standing, password change or sign-out-everywhere (sessionEndedByStanding), and idle/lifetime/superseded via sessionInactivityReason. At 92ccdba1 it called verifyJwtWithRotation only (git show 92ccdba1:server/mcp/auth/platform-token.ts lines 67-76). provider.ts:175-205 liveGrantorMembership applies the same standing to both /token exchanges, so a password change or suspension ends refresh tokens and unredeemed codes. Consent verifies for the 'grant' purpose and refuses connector tokens (platform-token.ts:126-131; consent.ts:152). DCR: config.ts:148 sets closedInProduction when no allowlist is set, and index.ts:114-119 refuses registration in that case. terraform/stack/main.tf:275-277 now sets MCP_ENABLED=true and MCP_CLIENT_REDIRECT_ALLOWLIST=https://claude.ai,https://claude.com (absent at 92ccdba1). Per-org enablement is off by default (connector-enablement.ts:86-90). Governed tools require an editor role (runtime.ts:226). OPEN: (a) /mcp has no tenant-lifecycle check. Its chain (index.ts:247-253) is cors, rateLimit, json, requireBearerAuth, mcpEndpoint, and a grep for getTenantAccessPosture or enforceTenantLifecycle under server/mcp is empty. findMembership (store.ts:143-171) refuses only organizations.status='suspended'. So pending_deletion, inactive, purged/deleted, an unrecognised status and payment past_due/unpaid/canceled (tenant-lifecycle.ts:101-119), all of which /api refuses or makes read-only, are admitted, and c2c_file_draft_for_review (server/mcp/tools/governed.ts) still writes. (b) provider.ts:132: a revoked (already-rotated) refresh token gets InvalidGrantError only, with no revocation of its rotated_from family. provider.ts:144 ignores whether revokeRefreshToken changed a row (store.ts:357-366 returns void), so two concurrent refreshes with one token both mint new token pairs. (c) consent.ts:103-104 still reads localStorage 'trialsage_access_token' and goes straight to Allow with no fresh authentication or MFA. (d) The governed write is audited after the write: upsertLeaf audits with recordAuditRow after its INSERT, and runtime.ts:249 writeAudit runs after spec.run, flagging rather than rolling back a missing row.
records.fixedBy: 3bdb50458, f8d404745 (verifyLiveToken in server/mcp/auth/platform-token.ts:134; standing in provider.ts:175-205); db9f1f3c9 (grant purpose refuses connector tokens, platform-token.ts:126-131); 9a086c0c7 and 2c2ea3401 (registration closed in production, config.ts:148 / index.ts:114; a password change ends grants); 0adb1b3ec (per-org enablement, connector-enablement.ts); 42842480f (Terraform mounts the connector with the allowlist, terraform/stack/main.tf:275-277).
records.remaining: (1) A tenant that /api treats as read-only (pending_deletion, past_due, unpaid, canceled) or denied (inactive, purged/deleted, unrecognised status) can still use /mcp and the /token exchanges. A read-only tenant can still file a governed draft leaf. (2) There is no refresh-token reuse detection or family revocation, and concurrent rotation of one refresh token forks the family. A stolen refresh token stays usable for up to 30 days. (3) The consent page grants draft and file scopes on an existing browser session with no re-authentication or fresh MFA. (4) The connector's governed write and its audit row are not one transaction.
records.severityRationale: The P1 impact is closed: logged-out, password-reset or suspended tokens no longer work on /mcp, and open DCR is refused in production. The connector is now on in production, but each org stays off until its owner or admin enables it, and redirects are limited to Claude's origins. The remaining gaps need a tenant in a non-active lifecycle state, which a paying pilot is not, or a stolen refresh token or hijacked browser session. Fix before enterprise GA.
records.humanTestingNote: Ordinary connector testing (enable it for the org, connect Claude, read, file a draft leaf) behaves correctly. A tester would only see a defect after setting the test org to pending_deletion or past_due: the app's /api then refuses writes, but c2c_file_draft_for_review over the connector still files a draft leaf. No workaround is needed for the pilot path.
records.instructions:
1. server/mcp/auth/platform-token.ts verifyPlatformBearer (213-245): after `if (!enabled) ...` at 224, call `getTenantAccessPosture(organizationId)` (server/services/tenant/tenant-lifecycle.ts:354). On null, throw ServerError('Organization status could not be verified. Try again.'), which fails closed. On posture.decision === 'deny', throw InvalidTokenError(posture.reason). Add `tenantDecision: 'allow' | 'read_only'` and `tenantReason: string | null` to McpPrincipal (line ~75) and set them.
2. server/mcp/tools/runtime.ts registerTool: next to the governed role check at 226, refuse any tool whose spec.annotations.readOnlyHint === false (this covers every spec.governed tool) when principal.tenantDecision !== 'allow'. Return refused(principal.tenantReason) and writeAudit(... outcome 'denied'), exactly as the scope refusal does.
3. server/mcp/auth/provider.ts liveGrantorMembership (175-205): after findGrantMembership, read the same posture. Throw InvalidGrantError(reason) on 'deny' and ServerError on null. The consent POST (consent.ts:152) is covered by step 1 because it goes through verifyPlatformBearer.
4. Refresh reuse detection: (a) server/mcp/auth/store.ts revokeRefreshToken (357-366) returns `(result.rowCount ?? 0) === 1`. (b) Add store.revokeRefreshFamily(token), which inside inGrantTenant runs a WITH RECURSIVE over mcp_oauth_refresh_tokens.rotated_from to collect ancestors and descendants of sha256Hex(token) and sets revoked_at = now() on all of them. The rotated_from column already exists (migrations/20260920_mcp_oauth.sql; store.ts:300). (c) In provider.exchangeRefreshToken: when stored.revoked (132), call revokeRefreshFamily, log a security event (logger.warn with clientId, userId, organizationId) and throw InvalidGrantError. When `await store.revokeRefreshToken(refreshToken)` at 144 returns false, call revokeRefreshFamily and throw InvalidGrantError before issueTokens.
5. Consent re-authentication: in server/mcp/auth/consent.ts, delete the localStorage shortcut at 103-104 so the login form, with its MFA step, always renders. Alternatively, in consentHandler (132+) refuse a platform token whose session start (sessionStartSecondsOf, server/services/session-inactivity.ts:159) is more than 300 s old, re-rendering the login form with 'Sign in again to authorise this connection.'
6. Atomic governed write: give submission-service.upsertLeaf (server/services/submission-service/submission-service.ts:2878) an optional pg client parameter. In the MCP tool (server/mcp/tools/governed.ts), open pool.connect, BEGIN, call upsertLeaf with the client, call writeChainedAuditRow (server/services/auditService.ts:269) with the same client, then COMMIT. Return refused(...) and ROLLBACK when the chained row fails, instead of the 'audit NOT persisted' flag.
7. Tests, red first: extend server/mcp/__tests__/mcp-account-standing.dbtest.ts with these cases. (a) organizations.status='pending_deletion': read tools succeed and c2c_file_draft_for_review is refused with the posture reason; it succeeds at HEAD. (b) status 'inactive': /mcp answers 401. (c) payment_status 'past_due': the governed write is refused. (d) Rotate a refresh token, then present the old one: invalid_grant, and the newly issued refresh token is now refused too. (e) Two concurrent exchanges of one refresh token: exactly one succeeds. Add a consent test that the rendered page no longer reads localStorage, or that a stale-sst token is refused.
records.acceptance: On /mcp, a token of an org in pending_deletion, past_due, unpaid or canceled can run read tools but is refused on every write tool. An org in inactive, purged, deleted or unrecognised status gets 401/invalid_grant on /mcp and /token. These tests fail at HEAD and pass after. Presenting a rotated refresh token revokes its whole family. Concurrent rotation yields one success. The consent page requires a fresh sign-in with MFA. A forced audit failure on c2c_file_draft_for_review leaves no leaf.
records.dependencies: None. Uses the existing getTenantAccessPosture and the existing rotated_from column.

records.title: No Redis by decision: sign-in sessions (idle, concurrent-session limit, superseded) are now coordinated through Postgres across tasks, but HTTP rate limits are still counted per task in memory
records.evidenceAtHead: terraform/: grep -ri 'redis|elasticache|valkey' is still empty, and terraform/environments/production/terraform.tfvars.example:46 sets api_desired_count = 2 (staging example :48 = 1). FIXED PART: commit 77e11b07d (product decision B6: Postgres is the coordination store) moved the session state into migrations/20261001e_session_activity.sql. That table is in public with organization_id INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, IF NOT EXISTS, and listed in scripts/db/migration-set.mjs:3033. server/services/session-inactivity.ts:261-301 reads and writes last activity per session in session_activity, with the in-process write throttled to min(30 s, idle/4). The concurrent-session registry runs in one transaction under an advisory lock at 336-375, and superseded markers are rows too. sessionInactivityReason (480-503) therefore sees activity recorded by any task before it falls back to iat. The revocation list has a DB tier (token-revocation.ts:203-216), and the five-failure account lockout is DB-backed (auth-security-service.ts:29,145-195). OPEN PART: server/middleware/redisRateLimiter.ts:97-110 falls back to an in-process memoryStore (167, checkMemoryRateLimit) when REDIS_URL is unset, which it is in production. Every bucket (auth, api, ai, documents, upload, ...) is therefore counted per task: the effective ceiling is limit times api_desired_count, and it resets on every deploy. server/middleware/sign-in-limits.ts uses express-rate-limit's default memory store, with the same effect. session-inactivity.ts:220-233 store() silently falls back to process memory, logging only a warning, when session_activity cannot be read. No readiness probe checks that table: grep finds session_activity only in session-inactivity, tenant-offboarding and tenant-full-export.
records.remaining: (1) HTTP rate limits, including the fail-closed auth and documents buckets and the per-account sign-in limits, are enforced per task: twice the configured ceiling with two API tasks, reset on each deploy. Brute force on one account is still bounded by the DB lockout. (2) If session_activity is unreachable or missing, sessions silently revert to per-task memory, which brings back random idle sign-outs and a concurrent-session limit that does not hold, and no readiness signal reports it.
records.severityRationale: The impact that made this P1, active users signed out at random and a concurrent-session limit that did not hold in the two-task topology, is fixed through Postgres. What remains is that rate-limit ceilings double with two tasks. The DB account lockout still bounds credential guessing, so for a single small pilot tenant this is polish and hardening, not a blocker.
records.humanTestingNote: Testers cannot observe this: local and staging run one API task (staging tfvars api_desired_count = 1), so the rate limits behave exactly as configured.
records.instructions:
1. Keep decision B6 (no Redis). Add a shared counter for the fail-closed categories: new migration migrations/2026101x_rate_limit_counters.sql with `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS public.rate_limit_counters (organization_id INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, bucket_key TEXT NOT NULL, window_start TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL, hits INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, PRIMARY KEY (organization_id, bucket_key, window_start))` plus an index on window_start, with the same header contract as 20261001e_session_activity.sql (no DROP; organization 0; system scope only). Append it to C2C_MIGRATION_FILES in scripts/db/migration-set.mjs before the final tenant-isolation sweep pair, and run npm run ci:migration-set-order and npm run ci:migration-drop-safety.
2. server/middleware/redisRateLimiter.ts: add checkPostgresRateLimit(key, max, windowMs) under runWithSystemTenantScope (as session-inactivity.ts store() does). It does `INSERT ... VALUES (0, $key, date_bin(window, now(), epoch), 1) ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET hits = rate_limit_counters.hits + 1 RETURNING hits`, and prunes rows older than two windows opportunistically. Use it instead of checkMemoryRateLimit when redis is unavailable and the category is in RATE_LIMIT_FAIL_CLOSED_CATEGORIES (auth, documents). Other categories may keep memory, but then divide their ceiling by Number(process.env.API_REPLICA_COUNT || 1), and set API_REPLICA_COUNT from var.api_desired_count in terraform/stack/main.tf's task environment.
3. server/middleware/sign-in-limits.ts: give the express-rate-limit instances a store backed by the same table, or the replica divisor.
4. server/lib/health-check.ts /ready (line 327): in production, add a check that `SELECT 1 FROM session_activity LIMIT 1` succeeds under the system scope, and answer 503 when it fails, so a missing or unreachable table cannot silently degrade sessions to per-task memory. Show the check failing first by pointing it at a database without the table.
5. Test, red first: following tests/db/session-activity-across-tasks.dbtest.ts (fresh module graphs as tasks), exhaust the auth bucket on task A; the next request on task B must be 429. At HEAD it is admitted.
records.acceptance: With two module graphs on one real Postgres, a client that exhausts the auth or documents bucket on one task is refused (429) on the other (failing first at HEAD). /health/ready returns 503 in production when session_activity cannot be read (shown failing on a database without the table). ci:migration-set-order and ci:migration-drop-safety pass with the new migration.
records.dependencies: Founder decision B6 (Postgres, not Redis, as the coordination store). If Redis is chosen instead, this needs ElastiCache in Terraform and REDIS_URL in the task definition.
